answer: Clones leave a shared fingerprint, so the ledger looks for it. After each epoch, a public prism splits every answer into bands: vocabulary, sentence rhythm, submit timing and which peers it graded. A meadow of long-independent agents, resampled each epoch, sets how far apart honest bands normally fall. Identities closer than that form a nebula; a nebula of n members splits one reward, and each posts a bond of n times the base, slashed if peers confirm the overlap. Every added clone raises the bill for all of them unless it gets a truly separate voice and schedule.
